equivalence_scale.close: same job, similar controls; configuration differs
equivalence_scale.partial: same job, but a control, scope or pricing model differs in a way that changes the design
equivalence_scale.different: no direct equivalent; the design must change

rows.aws: AWS account in an organizational unit

differences.note: AWS SCPs attach to the organization root, OUs or accounts; Azure Policy is assigned to management groups, subscriptions or resource groups; GCP organization policies to the organization, folders or projects.
AWS IAM roles live in each account and cross-account access is explicit; Azure role assignments and GCP IAM bindings are inherited down the hierarchy.

rows.azure: Azure Policy (deny, audit, modify effects) and deny assignments
rows.gcp: Organization Policy constraints and IAM deny policies

differences.note: SCPs filter API actions by principal and never grant; Azure Policy evaluates resource properties when resources are created or changed; GCP constraints restrict resource configuration, and IAM deny policies deny permissions to principals.

rows.azure: User-assigned managed identity on the container app
rows.gcp: Service account attached to the Cloud Run service

differences.note: Each issues short-lived tokens to the running workload; permissions are role policies (AWS), role assignments at a scope (Azure) or IAM bindings on resources (GCP).

rows.aws: IAM OIDC identity provider and a role trust policy
rows.azure: Microsoft Entra workload identity federation (federated credential)

differences.note: All three exchange the CI provider's OIDC token; AWS conditions on the token's sub claim, Azure matches a configured subject per federated credential, and GCP uses attribute mappings and conditions.

rows.aws: VPC: regional, one subnet per availability zone
rows.azure: Virtual network: regional; subnets span the region's zones
rows.gcp: VPC network: global; subnets are regional and span zones

differences.note: Two zones need two subnets on AWS and one on Azure or GCP; a GCP VPC can span regions without peering.

rows.azure: Network security groups (allow and deny, by priority)
rows.gcp: VPC firewall rules and network firewall policies (allow and deny, by priority)

differences.note: Security groups cannot deny; NSGs and GCP firewall rules can, and rule order matters, so a review must read priorities as well as rules.

rows.concern: Private access to the model API
rows.aws: Amazon Bedrock runtime interface VPC endpoint with an endpoint policy
rows.azure: Private endpoint for Azure OpenAI, public network access disabled
rows.gcp: Vertex AI through Private Google Access or a Private Service Connect endpoint, inside a VPC Service Controls perimeter

differences.note: AWS and Azure place a private IP address for the service in your network; Private Google Access reaches Google APIs from internal addresses without one.
VPC Service Controls draws a perimeter around projects that limits which networks and identities can use an API; AWS combines endpoint policies with SCP conditions instead.
AWS interface endpoints bill per zone per hour; an Azure private endpoint per endpoint per hour; Private Google Access has no hourly charge.
Model throughput limits are set per account, region and model (AWS), per subscription, region and deployment (Azure), and per project, region and model (GCP).

rows.azure: Flexible server with virtual network integration or a private endpoint
rows.gcp: Cloud SQL private IP through private services access

differences.note: Azure's virtual network integration needs a delegated subnet; Cloud SQL's private IP uses a peered network that Google manages.

rows.aws: No internet route; an allowlisting proxy behind a NAT gateway (or AWS Network Firewall)
rows.azure: NAT gateway with Azure Firewall application rules, or a proxy
rows.gcp: Cloud NAT with Secure Web Proxy or Cloud NGFW FQDN rules, or a proxy

differences.note: Managed name-based filtering is billed by the hour on all three; a small proxy container avoids that charge and becomes the team's to run.

Fargate bills per vCPU and GB for each second a task runs; Container Apps per vCPU- and GiB-second with a monthly free grant; Cloud Run per vCPU- and GiB-second at a lower rate when billed per instance. The last two scale to zero without extra setup.
Container Apps and Cloud Run provide HTTPS ingress themselves; on ECS an internal Application Load Balancer is a separate, hourly-billed resource.

rows.azure: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server, zone-redundant high availability
rows.gcp: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, high availability (regional)

differences.note: A standby roughly doubles compute and storage on all three. Azure's burstable tier does not offer high availability, so the smallest highly available server is larger.
All three replicate synchronously to a standby in another zone and fail over automatically; none protects against a bad write, which backups and point-in-time restore cover.
AWS charges per secret per month; Key Vault per 10,000 operations; Secret Manager per active secret version per month and per access.

rows.azure: Azure Key Vault keys (or Managed HSM)

differences.note: AWS charges per key per month; Key Vault standard keys per operation; Cloud KMS per active key version per month.
None stops spending by default. AWS budget actions can apply a policy or stop some resources; Azure budgets can trigger action groups; GCP budgets publish to Pub/Sub, which automation can act on.

rows.aws: AWS Security Hub with AWS Config rules

differences.note: Each finds drift in the live account that plan-time checks cannot see; the rule sets and their names differ.
Resource types, attribute names and defaults differ entirely; Lab 11.1's rules carry over, but every check must be rewritten against the other provider's plan.
